items.summary: In an interview with Italy's Corriere della Sera published Oct 20, Zelensky said Ukraine is ready for a mutual cessation of strikes on energy infrastructure, but pressed Washington directly: 'If you cannot restrain Putin, then give us interceptor missiles so I can protect our energy infrastructure.' He argued it is unfair for Ukraine to absorb Russian attacks on its grid without the means to retaliate or defend, and said Kyiv wants 'open, honest and pragmatic' relations with the US amid the rift over the diesel deal, Starshield limits and the stalled intel-sharing.
items.title: Zelensky tells Corriere della Sera Ukraine backs a mutual energy ceasefire — if the US supplies interceptor missiles to defend its grid

items.summary: Zelensky told US senators on Monday that the Pentagon is delaying delivery of air-defense missiles already paid for by European countries, with the shipment awaiting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature; he said several European countries are ready to transfer Patriot interceptors from their own stockpiles but are still awaiting US approval. Separately, the Washington Post, citing an unnamed Ukrainian official, reported Ukraine has 'only a couple' of Patriot interceptors left in stock and that the Trump administration has slowed approval for allies to transfer their own supplies — while Russian missile strikes on Ukraine's energy grid continue ahead of winter.
items.title: Zelensky says Pentagon is holding up European-paid air-defense missiles pending Hegseth's signature; WaPo says Kyiv has 'only a couple' of Patriot interceptors left
